notes.cutoff: Data cut-off: the EGX is closed on Friday and Saturday, so the latest close is Thursday 29 October (EGX30 49,596.14). Sunday 1 November is the first session after the CBE's 100 bp hike. Oil, US stocks and gold are Friday's closing levels. Bullish and bearish tags are directional reads of the news, not trade recommendations.
notes.unverified: Not verified and therefore left out or flagged: the Saudi deposit renewal comes only from unnamed banking sources, with no statement from the CBE or Saudi Arabia; the date of the post-hike T-bill auction is not stated by either report; Thursday's and Friday's debt flows; the budget's oil-price assumption; Egypt's October inflation figure; local gold prices (Egyptian sites give different 21-karat prices). Amwal Al Ghad's Thursday flow figures (foreign net buying of EGP 42.259 bn) disagree with Youm7 and Cairo Mubasher (EGP 29.2 bn), so the chart uses the two that agree. Cairo Mubasher puts gold at about $3,914 on Saturday morning against Kitco's late-Friday $3,879.90; the edition uses Kitco's dated closing quote.
notes.sourcesFoot: Not used: Amwal Al Ghad's Thursday flow figures (they conflict with two other sources); reports of the US ordering staff out of Saudi Arabia, which date from 21 to 23 October; and undated Egypt-Gaza-Sudan items. The BoJ and ECB decisions (29 and 30 October) appear only as rate references. The reserves figures (7 October) are the latest available. All 21 StockAnalysis pages were re-opened on Saturday and match across the same six sessions.

items: The CBE raises rates by 100 bp to a 20% deposit rate after Thursday's close, its first hike since March 2024, against a Reuters poll that expected a hold → the pound near record lows at EGP 56.12 and heavy foreign selling of local debt push the CBE to defend the carry trade; Sunday is the EGX's first session to price it.

EGX30 rises 0.64% to 49,596.14 on Thursday as Banque du Caire's EGP 36.37 bn offering executes and lifts turnover to EGP 43.9 bn → foreign institutions net buy EGP 29.2 bn, mostly through the bank's offering, while 180 stocks rise and 31 fall before trading in BQDC starts on 2 November.

The IMF targets a staff-level deal on Egypt's final review before mid-December, worth about $2.3 bn in final disbursements → Kozack says talks focus on tight monetary policy, which the CBE's hike now delivers.

Brent rises 1.04% to $116.08 in early Friday trade after settling at $114.88 on Thursday, as a tanker is hit in Hormuz and US strike talk returns → oil near $116 widens Egypt's fuel import bill while pump prices stay frozen.

The ECB and the Bank of Japan both hold, the BoJ at 1.25% by 8-1, while Reuters sources call a 17 December ECB hike all but certain → global policy stays tight after US growth beats forecasts at 3.4%, limiting appetite for emerging-market debt.

The CBE raises rates by 100 bp to a 20% deposit rate, its first hike since March 2024, when most analysts expected a hold → the pound's slide past 56 and about $1.67 bn of foreign and Arab debt selling in three days (derived) push the CBE to defend the carry trade.

The Fed holds at 3.75–4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with Cook and Hammack voting for a hike, and markets largely price a December hike → elevated inflation and war-driven uncertainty keep US yields high (10-year 5.04%), narrowing the carry that holds foreign money in Egyptian bills.

EGX30 closes Thursday 0.64% higher at 49,596.14 while the EGX70 jumps 2.77% → local buyers absorb foreign selling (foreign institutions net sell EGP 229.1 mn on Wednesday), leaving the index about 2.85% lower over five sessions (derived).
Foreign and Arab net selling of Egyptian bills and bonds slows to $391 mn on Wednesday from $619.1 mn → debt outflows continue but ease as the pound holds at EGP 56.20 at the CBE.

Banque du Caire's retail book closes 27 times covered and the sale is upsized to 45%, with trading expected on 2 November → EGP 49.2 bn of retail orders chase EGP 1.8 bn of stock, showing local appetite for quality state assets even in a falling market.

EGP passes 56 per dollar at the CBE (sell 56.3511 on Monday) as foreign and Arab investors net sell about $664 mn of bills and bonds → secondary-market debt selling and regional risk drive the slide; importers lose, USD earners gain, and Thursday's CBE meeting is the test.

EGX30 closes Monday at 48,416.94, down 8.4% in three sessions, and the FRA halves brokers' minimum liquid capital ratio to 5% → foreign selling and forced selling by leveraged holders prompt the regulator to ease the rule through Thursday.

Brent trades near $116 on Tuesday morning, about 55% above the $75 in Egypt's budget (derived) → Hormuz flows run at about 60% of normal and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia add supply fear, widening Egypt's fuel bill.

Egypt's parliament backs military support for Saudi Arabia while the Houthis keep firing at Riyadh and the Eastern Province → a closer link to the regional war lifts Egypt's risk premium and puts Suez and tourism sentiment at risk.

The Fed decides today with a hold priced at about 93% after September's hike to 3.75–4.00% → a firm Fed keeps foreign holders of Egyptian bills under pressure and leaves the CBE no room to cut on Thursday.
EGP breaks 56 per dollar at the CBE for the first time → foreign sellers of T-bills (net $700.5 mn on Monday) are the driver; importers and leveraged names suffer, USD earners gain.
EGX30 falls 1.66% to 48,416.94, down 8.4% in three sessions; EGX70 fell 11.07% on Sunday → liquidity, margin calls and foreign selling hit small caps hardest; Thursday's CBE meeting is the next test.

Parliament authorises Sisi to give military support to Saudi Arabia after Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport and Aramco sites → raises the regional risk premium on Egyptian assets and keeps Red Sea shipping risk alive for Suez revenue.
Brent sits at $115.41 while the US-Iran war keeps Hormuz under attack → Egypt's energy import bill and fuel subsidy gap widen just as the IMF's final review opens.

Banque du Caire prices its IPO at EGP 5.30 with the largest private tranche in EGX history → strong institutional demand helps the IMF divestment target but absorbs local liquidity before trading starts on 2 November.

top.why: a risk-off week end and forced selling of metals weigh on sentiment toward emerging markets before the EGX reopens.

stories.h: Brent hits a six-month high after a limpet-mine strike on a Hormuz tanker
stories.what: Brent's expiring December contract settles $2.76 higher at $117.64 after touching $118, and the more active January contract gains $2.63 to $113.43. WTI rises 2.08% to $104.12. Over October Brent gains 13.6% and WTI 15.2%, and both settle at their highest since late April. Explosives attached by a small boat hit a tanker in Hormuz, the first known successful limpet-mine strike since the war began in February.
stories.why: Traders expect escalation after the US midterms on 3 November. The Houthis claim strikes on Saudi sites including the Ras Tanura refinery, and an armed group shuts a Libyan pipeline valve, halting about 15,000 barrels a day.
stories.aff: Egypt's fuel import bill, the subsidy gap, freight costs and global inflation.
stories.eg: Higher crude raises the dollar cost of Egypt's fuel imports at a time when the pound sits near 56 per dollar.
stories.egx: Bearish for importers and energy-intensive industry; supportive for oil-linked names such as AMOC.

key.l: Saudi deposit renewed for a year, per banking sources

stories.h: Saudi Arabia renews a $5.3 bn deposit at the CBE for another year, sources say
stories.what: Riyadh agrees to keep a $5.3 bn deposit at the Central Bank of Egypt for one more year instead of taking it back when it falls due at the end of October, according to banking sources cited by Banker News and Khalf El Hadath. Saudi deposits at the CBE total about $10.3 bn, including $5 bn of short-term deposits renewed each year. Neither report cites a statement from the CBE or Saudi authorities.
stories.why: Gulf deposits are part of the support Egypt relies on while the Iran war hits Suez income and drives foreign money out of local debt.
stories.aff: Net international reserves ($57.35 bn at end-September), the pound and Egypt's external financing gap.
stories.eg: Banker News puts combined Saudi, Kuwaiti and Qatari deposits at about $18.3 bn.
stories.egx: Mildly bullish for the pound and foreign sentiment toward EGX blue chips, pending confirmation.

key.l: 364-day T-bill, first auction after the hike

stories.h: First T-bill auction after the hike lifts the 364-day yield to 26.08%
stories.what: The CBE accepts EGP 56.33 bn of 364-day bills at an average 26.076% (high 26.15%, low 25%) against a EGP 80 bn target, and EGP 22.51 bn of 182-day bills at 25.457% against EGP 30 bn. In total it takes EGP 78.84 bn, about $1.41 bn, or 71.7% of the EGP 110 bn target, from 1,830 bids. The 364-day yield was 25.912% at the 27 October auction.
stories.why: Thursday's 100 bp hike lifts the floor for bill yields as the state refinances.
stories.aff: Bank income, the state's interest bill and the carry trade for foreign investors.
stories.eg: Neither report gives the auction date or the share bought by foreign investors.
stories.egx: Bullish for banks' bill income; bearish for leveraged developers and NBFIs as funding costs rise.
stories.names: CIB, QNB Egypt, HDBK (bullish); TMG, Palm Hills (bearish).

stories.h: EGX30 ends October 0.64% higher as small caps lead and breadth turns strongly positive
stories.src: Amwal Al Ghad; Youm7; Cairo Mubasher; EnterpriseAM; StockAnalysis.com
stories.what: The EGX30 closes Thursday at 49,596.14, up 0.64%, after Wednesday's 1.64% fall. The EGX70 rises 2.77% to 16,779.72 and the EGX100 2.27% to 22,639.93. 180 stocks rise and 31 fall, and market cap gains about EGP 33 bn to EGP 3.892 tn. Beltone (+5.8%), AMOC (+4.9%) and Orascom Development (+3.7%) lead, while Abu Qir Fertilizers (-3.5%), Mopco (-2.5%) and Telecom Egypt (-1.7%) fall.
stories.why: None of the sources gives a single cause for the rise; the CBE's hike comes after the session. Flows are distorted by the Banque du Caire execution: foreign institutions net buy EGP 29.2 bn and Egyptian institutions net sell EGP 34.3 bn.
stories.aff: Small caps, brokers and the foreign-held blue chips that now face a higher rate environment.
stories.eg: EnterpriseAM puts the EGX30 up 18.6% year to date even after this month's sell-off.
stories.egx: Neutral overall: broad gains but fertiliser names and Telecom Egypt lag, and the rate hike is not yet priced.
stories.names: Beltone, AMOC, Orascom Development (up); Abu Qir, Mopco, Telecom Egypt (down).

key.l: Banque du Caire offering executed on the EGX

stories.h: Banque du Caire starts trading on Monday after its EGP 36.37 bn offering executes
stories.what: The public and private offering executes on Thursday for 6.862 bn shares, 45% of the bank's issued capital, at EGP 5.30, worth EGP 36.37 bn. The private placement of about 6.519 bn shares is worth about EGP 34.55 bn and was six times covered. Shares start trading on Monday 2 November as BQDC, valuing the bank at about EGP 80.83 bn.
stories.why: The sale was raised to 45% from 30% with the Financial Regulatory Authority's approval, and the retail tranche was heavily oversubscribed.
stories.aff: Brokerages, sentiment toward state-bank listings, the privatisation programme and local liquidity.
stories.eg: A completed sale of this size counts toward Egypt's asset-sale goals as the IMF programme nears its end.
stories.egx: Bullish for brokerages; the debut tests demand above the offer price.

stories.h: Analysts split on whether the CBE's hike will steady the pound
stories.what: The CBE raises its deposit rate to 20% and lending rate to 21% on Thursday, its first hike since March 2024, when a Reuters poll of 13 analysts expected a hold. Al Ain says foreign net sales of local debt topped $1 bn on 26 and 27 October. Madhat Nafeh says he expected the hike, citing outflows and energy prices, while Hany Genena of Al Ahly Pharos warns it carries a high cost for borrowers and public finances.
stories.why: The CBE cites challenging external conditions and wants to anchor inflation expectations as the pound trades near 56 per dollar.
stories.aff: The pound, T-bill yields, bank margins and borrowing costs across the economy.
stories.eg: Genena says a hike does not directly guarantee a weaker dollar, so the pound's path still depends on flows.
stories.egx: Sunday is the first session to price it: bullish for bank margins, bearish for developers, NBFIs and leveraged industrials.

key.l: S&P 500 on Friday, worst day since June

stories.h: Wall Street's worst day since June drags gold and silver lower
stories.what: The S&P 500 falls 1.8% to 7,580.07, the Dow 1.1% to 51,770.31 and the Nasdaq 2.9%. Intel drops nearly 29% after weak guidance and Amazon's spending plans weigh on tech. Gold falls 3.52% to about $3,879.90 and silver 6.06% to $49.015 in late trade, and the 10-year Treasury yield eases toward 4.93%.
stories.why: Worries about returns on AI spending trigger a tech sell-off, and investors sell metals to cover losses.
stories.aff: Global risk appetite, emerging-market flows and gold-linked savings.
stories.eg: Lower gold prices cut the value of Egyptians' gold savings and the gold share of CBE reserves.
stories.egx: Bearish for sentiment ahead of Sunday's open, especially growth and fintech names.

key.l: window for a possible US-Iran meeting in Doha or Istanbul

stories.h: Qatari mediators carry a Vance letter to Tehran as strike fears build
stories.what: Qatari mediators arrive in Tehran on Friday with a letter from US Vice President JD Vance to Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei. The letter reportedly proposes a "framework for negotiations" rather than peace terms, and a meeting could follow within a week in Doha or Istanbul. Iran has not formally replied.
stories.why: The Wall Street Journal reports Trump has told Gulf allies to prepare for a brief, high-intensity campaign after the midterms, which raises the stakes of the talks.
stories.aff: Oil, Gulf shipping, regional risk premiums and Suez traffic.
stories.eg: A deal would ease oil and shipping pressure on Egypt; escalation would do the opposite.
stories.egx: Neutral for now: the outcome swings oil, the pound and tourism sentiment.
